sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 38, recorded on July 28th, 2021.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 ADSP 播客第 38 期，录制于 2021 年 7 月 28 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we interview Sean Parent about the Adobe Software Technology Lab.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天和我一起主持的是布莱斯，我们采访了肖恩·帕伦特，聊聊 Adobe 软件技术实验室。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I guess this is the third.
sentences.zh: 对，所以我想这是第三个。

sentences.en: I mean, we've had, what, five episodes probably, but that was across two different recordings.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们大概做过五期左右，不过那是分两次录制的。

sentences.en: So at this point, probably most of our listeners know who you are, Sean.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，可能大部分听众都知道你是谁了，肖恩。

sentences.en: But in case there are some people that have tuned in since the last time that you were on,
sentences.zh: 但以防有些人是从你上次上节目之后才开始收听的，

sentences.en: maybe we'll start off by introduce, you can introduce yourself, just in case people are like, who is this, who is this Sean that has appeared out of nowhere?
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以先做个自我介绍，你可以介绍一下自己，以防有人在想：这是谁？这个凭空出现的肖恩是谁？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I'm Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 对，我是肖恩·帕伦特。

sentences.en: I'm a senior principal scientist at Adobe.
sentences.zh: 我是 Adobe 的高级首席科学家。

sentences.en: I've been at Adobe off and on a little bit, I guess, for over 25 years.
sentences.zh: 我在 Adobe 断断续续待了差不多有 25 年以上了。

sentences.en: Started on the Photoshop team, and most recently I've been working with the Photoshop team.
sentences.zh: 最早在 Photoshop 团队，最近一段时间也一直在和 Photoshop 团队合作。

sentences.en: And I'm restarting Adobe Software Technology Lab, which we'll talk more about in a bit here.
sentences.zh: 我正在重新组建 Adobe 软件技术实验室，我们待会儿会详细聊这个。

sentences.en: Before Adobe, I was at Apple for five years.
sentences.zh: 在 Adobe 之前，我在苹果待了五年。

sentences.en: I worked on QuickTry GX and then the transition to PowerPC.
sentences.zh: 我做过 QuickDraw GX，然后参与了向 PowerPC 的过渡。

sentences.en: And in the middle, somewhere close to the middle of my Adobe career, I took a year and went to Google and worked on Chrome OS and then flamed out and came back to Adobe.
sentences.zh: 中间，大概在我 Adobe 职业生涯的中期，我请了一年假去谷歌做了 Chrome OS，后来项目黄了，又回到了 Adobe。

sentences.en: So that's who I am.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的经历。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I think it was episode 16 or 17 was one of the first ones we had you on.
sentences.zh: 我想第 16 期或第 17 期是我们最早邀请你来上节目的其中一期。

sentences.en: And I believe you did talk about, what was it, the eight-year period with Alex Stepanov and was it Paul McJones?
sentences.zh: 我记得你当时确实聊过，是什么来着，和亚历克斯·斯特潘诺夫以及保罗·麦琼斯的八年合作？

sentences.en: That's where you had the initial ST lab, but like maybe you can recount briefly sort of that period of time.
sentences.zh: 那是你们最初建立 ST 实验室的地方，不过也许你可以简要回顾一下那段经历。

sentences.en: And you just sort of nonchalantly said that you're bringing it back, which is like, it's massive news.
sentences.zh: 你刚才轻描淡写地说你要把它带回来了，这可是个重磅新闻。

sentences.en: With Dave AbrahaMs.
sentences.zh: 和戴夫·亚伯拉罕斯一起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 好吧，你抢了他的风头，布莱斯。

sentences.en: Not going to cut that out.
sentences.zh: 这段我可不会剪掉。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 别介。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so this came about, I don't know, 2001, maybe.
sentences.zh: 所以，这大概是 2001 年左右萌生的。

sentences.en: Alex Stepanov came to Adobe and gave a talk.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·斯特潘诺夫来到 Adobe 做了一场演讲。

sentences.en: And after his talk, it was on STL.
sentences.zh: 演讲结束后，内容是关于 STL 的。

sentences.en: For people who don't know, Alex Stepanov is the person who created the standard template library for C++.
sentences.zh: 对于不了解的人来说，亚历克斯·斯特潘诺夫就是 C++ 标准模板库的创造者。

sentences.en: And he came and gave a talk at Adobe.
sentences.zh: 他来 Adobe 做了一场演讲。

sentences.en: And after his talk, he and I started chatting.
sentences.zh: 演讲结束后，我和他聊了起来。

sentences.en: And at the time, he was a vice president at Compaq, which was in transition.
sentences.zh: 当时他是康柏公司的副总裁，而康柏正处于转型期。

sentences.en: They had just been acquired by Hewlett-Packard.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚被惠普收购。

sentences.en: And so he was kind of sliding back to HP.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时正准备转回惠普。

sentences.en: He had actually created STL while working at HP Labs.
sentences.zh: 他其实是在惠普实验室工作期间创建了 STL。

sentences.en: And we were chatting about work that I was doing.
sentences.zh: 我们在闲聊我当时在做的工作。

sentences.en: And we ended up spending a long evening in my office just talking about engineering stuff.
sentences.zh: 结果我们在我的办公室里度过了漫长的一个晚上，一直在聊工程方面的事情。

sentences.en: And at the end, he said, you know, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 最后，他说，你知道，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I would love to get back into engineering.
sentences.zh: 我很想重新回到工程一线。

sentences.en: And I haven't had a conversation like this in a long time.
sentences.zh: 我好久没有过这样畅快的交流了。

sentences.en: And I said, well, why don't you?
sentences.zh: 我说，那你为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And just kind of shrugged it off.
sentences.zh: 当时也就随口一说。

sentences.en: But a couple weeks later, he called me up and said, you know, I gave it a lot of thought.
sentences.zh: 但几周后，他打电话给我说，你知道吗，我认真考虑过了。

sentences.en: And I don't want to be a manager anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不想再当管理者了。

sentences.en: I want to be an engineer.
sentences.zh: 我想成为一名工程师。

sentences.en: So is there a position at Adobe?
sentences.zh: 所以 Adobe 有这样的职位吗？

sentences.en: And there's a bit of a long story here.
sentences.zh: 这中间其实还有一段挺长的故事。

sentences.en: Because he did join Adobe.
sentences.zh: 因为他确实加入了 Adobe。

sentences.en: I was not able to get him to join.
sentences.zh: 但我当时没能把他弄进我所在的团队。

sentences.en: I was working in Adobe's research group.
sentences.zh: 我当时在 Adobe 的研发小组工作。

sentences.en: And I was not able to get him into Adobe's research group.
sentences.zh: 我没能把他拉进 Adobe 的研发小组。

sentences.en: So he joined a different group, one of our shared technology groups.
sentences.zh: 所以他加入了一个不同的团队，我们其中一个共享技术团队。

sentences.en: And found it a bit frustrating.
sentences.zh: 结果发现有点让人沮丧。

sentences.en: There was a bit of a mismatch there between somebody who's kind of a very senior researcher and mathematician.
sentences.zh: 一个非常资深的研发人员和数学家，跟一个天天忙着修各种 bug 的团队之间，存在一些错位。

sentences.en: And a group that's just slogging through a bunch of bugs.
sentences.zh: 而这带来的结果，你可以在亚历克斯的退休派对上听到我讲过这个故事。

sentences.en: And the result of that, you can find I gave this story at Alex's retirement party.
sentences.zh: 网上有那段视频。

sentences.en: So there's a video of that online.
sentences.zh: 也许你们可以在节目简介里放个链接。

sentences.en: Maybe you can link it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 但最终的结果是，我以为亚历克斯要辞职了。

sentences.en: But the end result was, I thought Alex was going to quit.
sentences.zh: 他当时越来越感到沮丧。

sentences.en: He was getting frustrated.
sentences.zh: 但他坚持认为，不，他觉得这份工作很有价值。

sentences.en: But he insisted that, no, he thought that the job was worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 而且他很享受。

sentences.en: And he was enjoying it.
sentences.zh: 他打算坚持下去，和他的团队一起把工作做好。

sentences.en: And he was going to stick it out and work with his team.
sentences.zh: 就在我们进行那次对话大约两周后，他打电话给我说，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: And about two weeks after we had that conversation, he called me up and said, guess what?
sentences.zh: 我说，你要辞职了。

sentences.en: And I said, you're quitting.
sentences.zh: 他说，没有，他们把我炒了。

sentences.en: He's like, no, they fired me.
sentences.zh: 就这样，他被 Adobe 解雇了。

sentences.en: And so he had been fired from Adobe.
sentences.zh: 我当时急得团团转。

sentences.en: And I scrambled.
sentences.zh: 然后格雷格·吉利，我想我之前提到过他。

sentences.en: And Greg Gilley, who I think I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我上次为了找他在台下唠叨的那段视频剪辑，可是花了整整 40 分钟。

sentences.en: I did spend like 40 minutes last time trying to find that video clip of him rambling on stage.
sentences.zh: 虽然花了我一段时间，但我确实找到了。

sentences.en: It took me a while, but I did find it.
sentences.zh: 你没找到吗？

sentences.en: You didn't find it?
sentences.zh: 我找到了。

sentences.en: I did find it.
sentences.zh: 我真的找到了。

sentences.en: I did find it.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: It's hilarious.
sentences.zh: 我希望听这档播客的人都能看到。

sentences.zh: 我理解。

sentences.en: I understand.

sentences.en: So in any case, I went to Greg.
sentences.zh: 格雷格当时是数字影像部门的总监。

sentences.en: Greg was director of digital imaging.
sentences.zh: 所以 Photoshop 和一大堆产品都在他手下，他跟我所在的部门不同，也和亚历克斯所在的部门不同。

sentences.en: So he had Photoshop and a bunch of products under him, different org than I was in and different organization than Alex was in.
sentences.zh: 但我跟格雷格很熟。

sentences.en: But I knew Greg well.
sentences.zh: 我去找格雷格说，这个人叫亚历克斯·斯特潘诺夫，我知道你可能甚至不知道他是谁，但他是一个极其优秀的人才。

sentences.en: And I went to Greg and I said, so this guy, Alex Stepanov, I know you probably don't even know who he is, but an amazing individual.
sentences.zh: 他刚被开除了。

sentences.en: He was just fired.
sentences.zh: 你得把他重新雇回来。

sentences.en: And you need to hire him back.
sentences.zh: 格雷格当时说，我不能这么做。

sentences.en: And Greg was like, I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个部门，这等于是在跟另一个副总裁抢人。

sentences.en: It's another organization that would be going against another VP.
sentences.zh: 我不能把这个人招回来。

sentences.en: I can't hire this guy back.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我这么跟你说吧。

sentences.en: And I said, well, I'll put it this way.
sentences.zh: 我说，如果他走，我也跟他一起走。

sentences.en: I said, if he goes, then I go with him.
sentences.zh: 所以你为什么不至少花点时间，出去跟这个人吃个午饭，看看你的看法呢？

sentences.en: And so why don't you at least take the time and go out to lunch and have lunch with the man and see what you think.
sentences.zh: 于是他去和亚历克斯吃了午饭，回来后打电话给我说，你来我办公室一趟。

sentences.en: And so he went to lunch with Alex and came back and called me and said, you know, come to my office.
sentences.zh: 我走进去，他说，你知道，真该死。

sentences.en: And I came in and he was, he said, you know, God damn you.
sentences.zh: 他说，我要，我要把这家伙招回来。

sentences.en: He said, I'm going to, I'm going to hire this guy back.
sentences.zh: 但他接着说，不过条件是这样的。

sentences.en: And he said, but here's the deal.
sentences.zh: 如果我把他招回来，你得管理他。

sentences.en: If I hire him back, you have to manage him.
sentences.zh: 就这样，亚历克斯和我创立了 Adobe 软件技术实验室，这个名字源于惠普软件技术实验室，实际上，

sentences.en: And so out of that, Alex and I started Adobe Software Technology Lab, which was, the name came from Hewlett Packard Software Technology Lab, which is actually,
sentences.zh: 每个人总是以为 STL 代表标准模板库（Standard Template Library）。

sentences.en: everybody always thinks that, you know, STL stands for a standard template library.
sentences.zh: 或者有些人认为它是 Stepanov 和 Lee 的缩写，因为那是亚历克斯·斯特潘诺夫和孟莉（Meng Lee）写的最初那篇论文。

sentences.en: Or some people think it's Stepanoff and Lee because it was, it was Alex Stepanoff and Meng Lee who wrote the, the initial paper.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，STL 来自软件技术实验室（Software Technology Lab），也就是亚历克斯在惠普工作的地方。

sentences.en: But it actually, STL comes from Software Technology Lab, which is where Alex was working at HP.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们创建了一个名为软件技术实验室的小组，它隶属于 Adobe 的数字影像组织。

sentences.en: And so, so we created a group, Software Technology Lab, and it was within Adobe's digital imaging organization.
sentences.zh: 该小组的宗旨是改进 Adobe 的软件工程实践。

sentences.en: And, and the charter of the group was to improve software engineering practice at Adobe.
sentences.zh: 但我们也认为，要做到这一点，你必须在全行业范围内推动。

sentences.en: But we also thought that to do that, you kind of had to do it industry wide.
sentences.zh: 我们将“实践”（practice）定义为区别于“流程”（process）的概念，这意味着我们关注的是工程师坐在键盘前敲下的代码是什么，

sentences.en: And we defined practice to be distinct from process, meaning that we were concerned with what engineers wrote when they sat down at the keyboard,
sentences.zh: 而不是他们如何运行 scrum，或者他们是否在遵循敏捷流程，又或是诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: not with things like how they ran a scrum or, or whether or not they were following an agile process or, or, or anything along those lines.
sentences.zh: 我们关注的是，当他们坐下来写代码时，他们到底在敲什么。

sentences.en: It was, it was, it was concerned about, you know, what do they actually type when they sit down and write code.
sentences.zh: 我们通过三个维度的策略来实现这一点。

sentences.en: And we did that with a three-prong approach.
sentences.zh: 首先一部分是教育。

sentences.en: So, part of it was, was education.
sentences.zh: 因此，亚历克斯当时在 Adobe 开设了一门课程。

sentences.en: And so, Alex was teaching a class at Adobe.
sentences.zh: 这最终促成了《编程珠玑》或是类似书籍的出版——那是亚历克斯和保罗·麦琼斯的书。

sentences.en: And that eventually led to the publication of Elements of Programming, which is, is Alex and Paul McJones, their, their book.
sentences.zh: 其中另一部分是库（Libraries）。

sentences.en: And, and, and part of it was libraries.
sentences.zh: 所以，除了教育，我们还有库和工具。

sentences.en: So, you know, besides education, we had libraries and tooling.
sentences.zh: 这催生了所谓的 Adobe 源库（Adobe Source Libraries），它们至今仍然活跃。

sentences.en: And so that, uh, uh, uh, created something called the Adobe Source Libraries, which are still kicking around.
sentences.zh: 它们已经转移到了我自己的域名下，也就是 stlab.cc。

sentences.en: They've kind of moved into my own domain, which is stlab.cc.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然可以在 GitHub 上找到，并且在 Adobe 内部得到了广泛使用。

sentences.en: And they're still available up on GitHub and still in wide use inside of Adobe.
sentences.zh: 不过，这是一套做了一些有趣事情的库，我们以后有机会可以聊聊。

sentences.en: Uh, uh, uh, but that's, you know, a set of libraries that do some interesting things that we could talk about at some point.
sentences.zh: 还有一部分是研究。

sentences.en: And then part of it was research.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们与各大高校保持着长期的合作，包括安德鲁·莱姆斯坦所在的印第安纳大学，以及比雅尼·斯特劳斯特鲁普所在的德州农工大学。

sentences.en: So we had ongoing collaborations with, uh, uh, universities, including Indiana University, where Andrew Lemstein was at, and Texas A&M, where Bjarne Struistrup was at.
sentences.zh: 我们还请来了保罗·麦琼斯，对于不了解的人来说，保罗在这一行已经很久了。

sentences.en: Um, uh, uh, uh, and we brought in Paul McJones, who, uh, for people who don't know, Paul's been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 他曾在 IBM 与约翰·巴库斯共事。

sentences.en: He worked with John Backus, uh, at IBM.
sentences.zh: 他参与过模块三语言（Module 3）以及早期关系型数据库 System R 的工作。

sentences.en: He worked on the, the, uh, worked on the module three language, uh, uh, system R, which was an early relational database.

sentences.en: Um, John Backus, for those that don't know, so he's got, I think is, uh, that's the individual who was behind Fortran?
sentences.zh: 开发了 Fortran 的个人，图灵奖得主。

sentences.en: Uh, individual who's behind Fortran, uh, Turing Award winner.

sentences.en: Um, uh, if you've ever heard of, of EPNF as a way to describe grammars, that's, that's, uh, Backus is the B in EPNF.

sentences.en: Um, so yes.

sentences.en: Quite prolific.

sentences.en: Uh, one of the, one of the greats in the industry.

sentences.en: So kind of the peak of the group, there were five of us.

sentences.en: Uh, and we had a good, good eight-year run, and then had kind of a spectacular, very political, uh, flame out at the end of the eight years.

sentences.en: And that led to me resigning, and that's how I ended up at Google for a while.
